# Phase One — Chesed: Unlimited SEO and UX Brainstorm

The Awtsmoos pours possibility like an endless living sea,
Awtsmoos.com may hide immense machinery beneath a surface plain and free.
This pass refuses premature restraint and maps the fullest field in sight,
Then Gevurah will measure every vessel so abundance becomes usable light.

## Search discovery possibilities

- Central metadata registry keyed by canonical route families.
- Initial-HTML titles, descriptions, canonicals, robots, Open Graph, Twitter cards, and language metadata.
- Valid route-aware JSON-LD builders: WebSite, Organization, WebPage, CollectionPage, ItemList, BreadcrumbList, Article, ProfilePage, SoftwareApplication, VideoGame, and discussion types only where visible content supports them.
- One canonical URL normalizer stripping tracking noise while preserving meaningful identity.
- Semantic breadcrumbs from route meaning rather than raw path segments.
- Human discovery hubs linking apps, games, Torah, Heichelos, docs, and other public districts.
- Sitemap coverage derived from a safe public-route catalog rather than hand-maintained drift.
- Explicit noindex policy for auth, mutation, private workspace, ephemeral state, and internal tooling.
- Deterministic social-card fallbacks and real hreflang only where translations exist.
- One meaningful H1, HTML landmarks, descriptive anchors, crawlable summaries, useful 404 recovery, and real freshness metadata only where timestamps exist.
- Image alt text, dimensions, lazy loading, and priority hints based on actual importance.
- Canonical pagination, stable public content identities, crawler-readable SSR, and crawl-budget protection from parameter explosions.

## UX simplicity possibilities

- One obvious primary action per public surface.
- Compact shared navigation with a few top-level destinations.
- Search as the universal discovery affordance, backed by rich route/content knowledge underneath.
- Progressive disclosure for advanced controls.
- Consistent content width, spacing, typography, focus states, and tap targets.
- Reusable public page shell: skip link, header, breadcrumbs, main landmark, related links, footer.
- Mobile-first navigation with one simple disclosure instead of dense menus.
- Less visual chrome and fewer competing cards above the fold.
- Content-first pages, explicit loading/empty/error states, keyboard-first focus, reduced motion, predictable back/home paths, and simple cards with title/purpose/one action.

## Complexity underneath

- SEO domain layer: route classifier, metadata resolver, structured-data resolver, canonical resolver, renderer.
- UI domain layer: route taxonomy, primary-action model, navigation registry, related-content resolver.
- Semantic contracts independent of styling.
- Raw-response crawler checks before hydration.
- Desktop/tablet/mobile browser matrix and performance budgets.
- Accessibility contracts for landmarks, heading order, labels, focus, and touch targets.
- A public-route manifest reused by sitemap, navigation, SEO, docs, and tests.

## Five competing architectures

### A — Per-page hand tuning
Maximum specificity; maximum drift. Reserve for exceptional pages only.

### B — Central client-side SEO injector
Easy retrofit; too weak as primary crawler strategy because metadata arrives after initial HTML.

### C — Central server/static route metadata registry
Strong default: one source can serve head output, sitemap seeds, breadcrumbs, and tests.

### D — Template-owned metadata factories
Strong semantic locality: templates own dynamic facts while a shared renderer owns mechanics.

### E — Hybrid registry plus template factories
Likely strongest: registry owns taxonomy/crawl policy; templates own dynamic content facts; shared renderers output metadata and structured data.

## First-pass preference

Architecture E best matches "simple surface, complexity underneath," but no commitment is valid until route and template archaeology proves the integration points.
